newsitem.title: USA: Central Illinois to see little weekend rainfall.
newsitem.headline: Central Illinois to see little weekend rainfall.

text.p: Showers were expected this weekend across the eastern U.S. Midwest but meteorologists said Saturday that coverage would be thin across dry portions of central Illinois.

"It looks like there's going to be a frontal boundary sticking around that area (central Illinois) for the next few days," said Joel Wiedenor, staff meteorologist with CROPCAST. "It will trigger off a few showers with maybe 30 percent coverage. It looks like it's going to be damp but no widespread rains to bring any real relief."
Recent rains have bypassed central Illinois, leaving some corn and soybean fields in dire need of moisture.

"They're going to be faced with some scattered showers and thunderstorms," said Larry Mack, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp. "Some areas will get hit pretty good and other areas won't get anything. The best precipitation will be in northern Illinois."

Mack put rainfall amounts in northern Illinois at 0.50 to one inch with 60 percent coverage. He put coverage closer to 30 percent for central and southern Illinois with rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 0.75 inch through Monday.

"It looks like the northern fourth of Illinois should see some good rain over the next 36 hours," a meteorologist with Weather Express Inc said. "The southern part of the state will probably have to wait until Monday afternoon or Tuesday before they see a good chance."
Northern Illinois has already received heavy rainfall this weekend. Strong wind and thunderstorms late Friday and early Saturday downed tree limbs and power lines.
